title_en: Chongqing Municipal People's Government & Chongqing Liangjiang Volunteer Service Development Center v. Chongqing Cangjinge Property Management Co., Ltd. & Chongqing Shouxu Environmental Protection Technology Co., Ltd. — dispute over environmental pollution liability
ruling_gist_en: I. During the trial of an environmental public interest lawsuit, if a provincial people's government files an ecological and environmental damage compensation lawsuit regarding the same pollution facts, and the two cases have the same factual basis, identical litigation purposes, the same defendants, and substantially similar claims, the two cases may be consolidated for trial.

full_text_en:
Chongqing Municipal People's Government and Chongqing Liangjiang Volunteer Service Development Center v. Chongqing Cangjinge Property Management Co., Ltd. and Chongqing Shouxu Environmental Technology Co., Ltd. — Dispute over Environmental Pollution Liability

【Ruling Summary】

I. During the trial of an environmental public interest litigation, where a provincial-level people's government files an ecological environment damage compensation lawsuit against the same pollution incident, and where the two cases share identical facts, the same litigation purpose, the same defendants, and substantially similar claims, the two cases may be consolidated for trial.

II. Where environmental pollution conduct has already been adjudicated through criminal and administrative proceedings, facts confirmed by effective judgments may be directly admitted as evidence in ecological environment damage compensation lawsuits and environmental public interest litigations. However, due to differences in the standards of proof and burden of proof, the facts ultimately found by the court, provided there is no conflict, may differ from those found in criminal and administrative cases.

III. Given the concealment of the principal's intent to cause harm in principal-agent-type environmental torts, the determination of the subjective joint intent of the principal and agent to commit a tort may be inferred by comprehensively assessing factors such as the statutory duty of the discharging entity, the illegality of the conduct, the tacit understanding between the parties, and their objective cooperation.

IV. Where polluted water bodies are in a flowing state, making direct calculation of the amount of ecological environment damage difficult, the virtual abatement cost method may be used to quantify the damage consequence. That is, the actual unit abatement cost is taken as the unit virtual abatement cost, and multiplied by the volume of illegally discharged pollutants to calculate the quantified amount of ecological environment damage. The tortfeasor's liability is satisfied through alternative restoration.

V. In ecological environment damage compensation lawsuits and environmental public interest litigations, reasonable expenses such as attorney's fees and appraisal fees shall be supported. Where the plaintiff claims attorney's fees or appraisal fees supported only by contracts but not by invoices, the local government's guidance price may be used as a reference standard for determining the reasonableness of such expenses.

Plaintiff: Chongqing Municipal People's Government, domiciled at Renmin Road, Yuzhong District, Chongqing.
Legal Representative: Zhang Guoqing, Mayor of the Municipality.
Designated Representative: Chongqing Environmental Protection Bureau, domiciled at Qishan Road, Ranjiaba, Yubei District, Chongqing.

Plaintiff: Chongqing Liangjiang Volunteer Service Development Center, domiciled at Yuzhou Road, Jiulongpo District, Chongqing.
Legal Representative: Xiang Chun, Director of the Center.

Defendant: Chongqing Cangjinge Property Management Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Cangjinge Company), domiciled at Gangning, Jiangbei District, Chongqing.
Legal Representative: Sun Qiliang, Chairman of the Board.

Defendant: Chongqing Shouxu Environmental Technology Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Shouxu Company), domiciled at Innovation Avenue, Jiulongpo District, Chongqing.
Legal Representative: Cheng Long, General Manager of the Company.

Plaintiff Chongqing Municipal People's Government filed a lawsuit against Defendant Chongqing Cangjinge Property Management Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Cangjinge Company) concerning a dispute over environmental pollution liability, which was docketed by the First Intermediate People's Court of Chongqing on June 2, 2017. On July 5, 2017, the Chongqing Municipal People's Government applied to add Chongqing Shouxu Environmental Technology Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Shouxu Company) as a defendant, which was granted after examination. The First Intermediate People's Court of Chongqing separately accepted another case filed by Plaintiff Chongqing Liangjiang Volunteer Service Development Center against Defendants Cangjinge Company and Shouxu Company concerning a dispute over environmental pollution liability. After docketing, the case was tried under ordinary procedure, and the acceptance was publicly announced within the statutory period. Since the Chongqing Municipal People's Government and the Chongqing Liangjiang Volunteer Service Development Center filed lawsuits based on the same facts, with the consent of all parties, the First Intermediate People's Court of Chongqing decided on July 26, 2017 to consolidate the two cases for trial.

Plaintiffs Chongqing Municipal People's Government and Chongqing Liangjiang Volunteer Service Development Center alleged:

The Chongqing Cangjinge Electroplating Industrial Park (also known as Cangjinge Electroplating Industrial Center) is located within the Gangcheng Industrial Park in Jiangbei District, Chongqing. Wastewater generated by electroplating enterprises in the park was to be treated by the wastewater treatment station of Defendant Cangjinge Company. In December 2013, Cangjinge Company and Defendant Shouxu Company entered into an "Agreement for the Commissioned Operation of the Electroplating Wastewater Treatment Project" (hereinafter referred to as the "Commissioned Operation Agreement"), under which Shouxu Company undertook the operation of the wastewater treatment project at the Cangjinge Electroplating Industrial Center. On April 21, 2016, during an on-site inspection of Cangjinge Company's wastewater treatment station, law enforcement officers from the Chongqing Environmental Monitoring Corps discovered that two total chromium reactors and one comprehensive reactor facility at the treatment station were not in operation, and that production wastewater was being discharged into the external environment without treatment. From April 22 to 26, 2016, sampling and monitoring analysis by law enforcement officers revealed that the discharged wastewater contained heavy metals exceeding standards, with a total chromium concentration of 55.5 mg/L, total zinc concentration of 2.85×10² mg/L, total copper concentration of 27.2 mg/L, and total nickel concentration of 41 mg/L, exceeding the standards set out in the "Emission Standard for Electroplating Pollutants" (GB21900-2008) by 54.5 times, 189 times, 53.4 times, and 81 times, respectively, causing significant impact and damage to the ecological environment. On May 4, 2016, during another on-site inspection, law enforcement officers discovered that wastewater from Cangjinge Treatment Station's No. 1 comprehensive wastewater conditioning tank was being directly discharged, via a 120 mm diameter pipeline on the tank wall, without treatment, into the Gangcheng Park municipal wastewater pipeline network and then into the Yangtze River. Monitoring showed that the leaked wastewater in Tank No. 1 had a hexavalent chromium concentration of 6.10 mg/L and a total chromium concentration of 10.9 mg/L, exceeding the national standards by 29.5 times and 9.9 times, respectively. According to the investigation, from September 2014, Cangjinge Company and Shouxu Company, knowing that a 120 mm pipeline in the No. 1 comprehensive wastewater conditioning tank connected to the municipal wastewater pipeline network and could directly discharge into the Yangtze River, nonetheless used that pipeline to directly discharge untreated heavy metal-containing wastewater into the Yangtze River. The total volume of illegally discharged wastewater from September 1, 2014 to May 5, 2016 was 145,624 tons. Regarding the illegal conduct of Cangjinge Company and Shouxu Company in discharging wastewater and causing serious ecological damage, the Chongqing Environmental Monitoring Corps, based on the holder of the pollutant discharge permit, imposed a surcharge for the discharge fee and a fine on Cangjinge Company. Cangjinge Company and Shouxu Company intentionally used a concealed pipe to discharge超标 (above-standard) wastewater. Their illegal conduct was long-lasting, involved a large volume of discharge, and the environmental impact of the pollutants on the mainstream of the Yangtze River and downstream ecological areas was in a state of diffusion, making the extent of the ecological damage incalculable. Commissioned by the Chongqing Municipal People's Government, the Chongqing Academy of Environmental Sciences conducted an appraisal and assessment, concluding that the ecological environment damage costs caused by the two defendants' illegal discharge of超标 (above-standard) wastewater amounted to RMB 14,416,776.

The illegally discharged wastewater flowed into the Yangtze River, causing serious ecological damage, for which the two defendants shall be jointly and severally liable. Cangjinge Company, as a legal person specifically established to bear the discharge liability for the Cangjinge Electroplating Industrial Park where it is located, and as the entity that obtained the pollutant discharge permit for its wastewater treatment station, shall bear tort liability for the environmental damage caused by wastewater discharged from its treatment station. Shouxu Company, by entering into the Commissioned Operation Agreement with Cangjinge Company, became the entity responsible for the daily operation and maintenance of the said wastewater treatment station. It was also the direct actor that knowingly used the 120 mm diameter pipeline on the wall of the No. 1 comprehensive wastewater conditioning tank to illegally discharge heavy metal-containing wastewater, and shall bear tort liability for the environmental damage caused by the illegal discharge. The two defendants had subjective knowledge and joint intention regarding the existence of the unsealed 120 mm diameter pipeline on the wall of the No. 1 comprehensive wastewater conditioning tank and its use for illegally discharging heavy metal-containing wastewater, constituting a joint tort. Therefore, the two defendants shall be jointly and severally liable for the ecological environment damage caused. Furthermore, environmental tort liability follows the principle of no-fault liability. Regardless of whether the polluter had subjective knowledge or intentional fault, pursuant to Article 5 of the *Interpretation of the Supreme People's Court on Several Issues Concerning the Application of Law in the Trial of Disputes over Environmental Tort Liability*, Cangjinge Company cannot assert a reduction or exemption from its own compensation liability on the ground that Shouxu Company committed the illegal discharge. Additionally, according to Article 22 of the *Interpretation of the Supreme People's Court on Several Issues Concerning the Application of Law in the Trial of Environmental Civil Public Interest Litigations*, the two defendants shall bear the appraisal fees and attorney's fees in this case. The plaintiffs requested the court to order: 1. The two defendants to jointly and severally compensate for the ecological environment damage costs of RMB 14,416,776 resulting from the illegal discharge of above-standard wastewater polluting the water environment, to be used for off-site alternative restoration; 2. The two defendants to bear the ecological environment damage appraisal and assessment fees of RMB 300,000 in this case; 3. The two defendants to bear the litigation costs of this case and the attorney's fees separately incurred by the Chongqing Municipal People's Government and the Chongqing Liangjiang Volunteer Service Development Center, amounting to RMB 198,000 and RMB 80,000, respectively. Furthermore, during the trial, the Chongqing Liangjiang Volunteer Service Development Center added a claim for the two defendants to make a public apology.

Defendants Cangjinge Company and Shouxu Company argued:

The plaintiffs' allegations regarding the types of pollutants, the exclusivity of the pollution source, and the volume of illegally discharged wastewater are erroneous and are not admitted.

1. Error concerning the types of pollutants. The "Appraisal and Assessment Report on the Ecological Environment Damage Caused by the Illegal Wastewater Discharge Case of Chongqing Cangjinge Property Management Co., Ltd." (hereinafter referred to as the "Appraisal Report") submitted by the plaintiffs states that the main pollution factors include hexavalent chromium, total chromium, total zinc, total nickel, and other heavy metals. This is inconsistent with the actual on-site situation. Cangjinge Treatment Station's No. 1 conditioning tank (total chromium wastewater conditioning tank) contains only chromium heavy metals; the No. 2 conditioning tank (comprehensive wastewater conditioning tank) treats copper, nickel, and zinc wastewater. Only the No. 1 conditioning tank was ever used for illegal discharge; the No. 2 conditioning tank was not. The judgment in Case No. (2016) Yu 0112 Xing Chu 1615 of the Yubei District People's Court of Chongqing states that, according to sampling and testing by the Jiangbei District Environmental Monitoring Station, the wastewater leaked from the No. 1 conditioning tank exceeded the standard for hexavalent chromium and total chromium.

2. Error concerning the exclusivity of the pollution source. The analysis report No. Jiang Huan (Jian) Zi [2016] No. JD009 issued by the Jiangbei District Environmental Monitoring Station of Chongqing shows that wastewater sampling points included W4 and W6, both of which are at a higher elevation than the treatment station. It is impossible for water from the treatment station to flow backward to those points. Therefore, the pollutants did not originate from the Cangjinge treatment station, and the determination of the pollution source as exclusive is erroneous.

3. Inaccurate measurement of illegally discharged wastewater. The illegal discharge was not through a direct discharge via a 120 mm pipe, but rather through several small holes less than 9 cm in width and 0.5-1 cm in height, resulting in leakage. The total cross-sectional area of the holes was less than 5 cm², located 1.5 m above the tank floor, with no pressure, calculating only the gravity flow rate. The leakage volume is calculated as flow velocity × cross-sectional area × soil permeability after compaction = leakage volume. Based on this, the leakage flow rate is 0.2 m/s × 5 cm² × 10% = 0.036 m³/h. The plaintiffs' allegation of an instantaneous discharge of 140,000 tons of wastewater is unfounded.

4. Error concerning the determination of damage. While the illegal discharge did occur, the plaintiffs have not produced conclusive evidence that actual damage occurred. No evidence has been presented regarding changes in water quality, reduction in species, or changes in soil along the banks of the Yangtze River. Instead, the plaintiffs inferred the damage based solely on the discharge conduct. Moreover, the calculation of the damage amount is inaccurate. The Commissioned Operation Agreement between the two defendants stipulated a unit price of RMB 15/ton. The appraisal institution calculated an average of RMB 22/ton based on the total payment over the period, then multiplied by 4.5 times to calculate the unit cost of the damage amount, which clearly inflates the damage figure.

Cangjinge Company further argued that it had entered into a Commissioned Operation Agreement with Shouxu Company, and the illegal discharge was the act of Shouxu Company, unrelated to Cangjinge Company. Therefore, Shouxu Company should bear civil liability, and Cangjinge Company should not be held liable for compensation.

The First Intermediate People's Court of Chongqing found at first instance:

The Chongqing Cangjinge Electroplating Industrial Park was established in 2005, located within the Gangcheng Industrial Park in Jiangbei District, Chongqing. It was the only electroplating industrial park in the Gangcheng Industrial Park. The electroplating industrial park was a government-approved centralized electroplating industrial processing zone, housing several electroplating enterprises. Defendant Cangjinge Company was established in July 2012 to provide property management services for the enterprises in the park and to handle the treatment of wastewater generated by these enterprises. Cangjinge Company obtained a pollutant discharge permit and owned facilities and equipment for wastewater treatment. On December 5, 2013, Cangjinge Company and Defendant Shouxu Company entered into a four-year Commissioned Operation Agreement, under which Shouxu Company undertook the wastewater treatment project at the Cangjinge Electroplating Industrial Center. The wastewater from the electroplating center was handed over by Cangjinge Company to Shouxu Company for treatment using the wastewater treatment equipment owned by Cangjinge Company. On April 21, 2016, during an on-site inspection of Cangjinge Company's wastewater treatment station, law enforcement officers from the Chongqing Environmental Monitoring Corps discovered that two total chromium reactors and one comprehensive reactor facility at the treatment station were not in operation, and that production wastewater was being discharged into the external environment without treatment. From April 22 to 26, 2016, sampling and monitoring analysis by law enforcement officers revealed that the discharged wastewater contained heavy metals exceeding standards, with a total chromium concentration of 55.5 mg/L, total zinc concentration of 2.85×10² mg/L, total copper concentration of 27.2 mg/L, and total nickel concentration of 41 mg/L, exceeding the standards set out in the *Emission Standard for Electroplating Pollutants* (GB21900-2008) by 54.5 times, 189 times, 53.4 times, and 81 times, respectively, causing significant impact and damage to the ecological environment. On May 4, 2016, during another on-site inspection, law enforcement officers discovered that heavy metal-containing wastewater from Cangjinge Treatment Station's No. 1 comprehensive wastewater conditioning tank was being directly discharged, via a 120 mm diameter pipeline on the tank wall, without normal treatment, into the external environment, then into the Gangcheng Park municipal pipeline network, and finally into the Yangtze River. Monitoring showed that the leaked wastewater in Tank No. 1 had a hexavalent chromium concentration of 6.10 mg/L and a total chromium concentration of 10.9 mg/L, exceeding the national standards by 29.5 times and 9.9 times, respectively. The total volume of illegally discharged wastewater from September 1, 2014 to May 5, 2016 was 145,624 tons.

It was further found that in August 2014, Cangjinge Company converted the original waste acid collection tank into the No. 1 comprehensive wastewater conditioning tank, and changed the wastewater conveyance from an underground pipeline system to an overhead pipeline system. The tank originally had one 110 mm diameter pipeline and one 120 mm diameter pipeline on its wall. During the conversion, only the 110 mm diameter pipeline was sealed; the 120 mm diameter pipeline was not sealed. This unsealed pipeline was underground and concealed. From September 2014, Shouxu Company, knowing that there was a 120 mm pipeline in the tank that connected to the external environment, nonetheless continued to use that pipeline to directly discharge untreated heavy metal-containing wastewater into the external environment.

Commissioned by the Chongqing Municipal People's Government, the Chongqing Academy of Environmental Sciences conducted an appraisal and assessment of the ecological environment damage caused by the illegal discharge of above-standard wastewater by Defendants Cangjinge Company and Shouxu Company, and issued the "Appraisal Report" in April 2017. The appraisal report states: In this incident, the pollution conduct is clear, the pollutant migration pathway is reasonable, the pollution source is homologous to the pollutants in the illegally discharged wastewater, and the pollution source is exclusive. The pollution conduct persisted from September 1, 2014 to May 5, 2016, with a total of 145,624 tons of wastewater illegally discharged. The main pollution factors were hexavalent chromium, total chromium, total zinc, total nickel, etc., causing serious damage to the water body of the Yangtze River. The Appraisal Report used the virtual abatement cost method, recommended by the *General Guidelines for Technical Assessment of Ecological Environment Damage* and the *Recommended Methods for Environmental Damage Assessment (Version II)*, to quantify the ecological environment damage. It took the actual treatment cost of RMB 22/ton as the unit virtual abatement cost, multiplied by the volume of illegally discharged wastewater, to calculate the virtual abatement cost as RMB 3,203,728. The discharge point of the illegal wastewater was in the main urban section of the Yangtze River mainstream, which falls under Class III water body functions. According to the "Principles for Determining Pollution Remediation Costs" under the virtual abatement cost method, the multiplier range for Class III water bodies is 4.5 to 6 times the virtual abatement cost. For this assessment, the lowest multiplier of 4.5 was chosen, ultimately assessing the quantified amount of ecological environment pollution damage caused by the two defendants' illegal discharge as RMB 14,416,776 (i.e., RMB 3,203,728 × 4.5 = RMB 14,416,776). The Chongqing Academy of Environmental Sciences is an appraisal institution confirmed in the *Notice of the Ministry of Environmental Protection on Printing and Issuing the List of Recommended Institutions for Environmental Damage Assessment (First Batch)*. On June 30, 2016, the Chongqing Environmental Monitoring Corps issued an administrative penalty decision, fining Cangjinge Company RMB 5,807,200, on the grounds that from September 1, 2014 to May 5, 2016, Cangjinge Company had directly discharged heavy metal-containing wastewater into the Gangcheng Park municipal wastewater pipeline network and then into the Yangtze River through the 120 mm diameter pipeline in the No. 1 comprehensive conditioning tank, bypassing the general outlet of the wastewater treatment station. Cangjinge Company applied for administrative reconsideration to the Chongqing Environmental Protection Bureau, which issued a reconsideration decision upholding the administrative penalty. Cangjinge Company then sued to the Yubei District People's Court of Chongqing, seeking to have the administrative penalty decision and reconsideration decision revoked. On February 28, 2017, the Yubei District People's Court of Chongqing rendered Administrative Judgment (2016) Yu 0112 Xing Chu No. 324, dismissing Cangjinge Company's claims. Cangjinge Company did not appeal, and the judgment became legally effective.

On November 28, 2016, the Chongqing Yubei District People's Procuratorate filed a public prosecution with the Chongqing Yubei District People's Court, alleging that Shouxu Company had undertaken the entrusted operation project for electroplating wastewater treatment of Cangjin Pavilion Company, and illegally discharged electroplating wastewater that had not been treated up to standard directly into the external environment. Shouxu Company, Cheng Long (legal representative of Shouxu Company), and others were accused of constituting the crime of environmental pollution and should be investigated for criminal liability according to law. The Chongqing Yubei District People's Court, on December 29, 2016, rendered a criminal judgment (〔2016〕Yu 0112 Xing Chu No. 1615), finding Shouxu Company guilty of the crime of environmental pollution, sentenced it to a fine of RMB 80,000; Cheng Long and others were found guilty of the crime of environmental pollution and were sentenced to fixed-term imprisonment ranging from nine months to six months, and fines ranging from RMB 40,000 to RMB 10,000. After the judgment was rendered, no protest nor appeal was filed, and the judgment became legally effective.

Separately found: The plaintiff, Chongqing Liangjiang Volunteer Service Development Center, was established in 2011 and is a social organization primarily engaged in various public welfare activities such as environmental protection, cultural education, and disaster relief, under the supervision of the Chongqing Municipal Spiritual Civilization Construction Committee.

First instance of the Chongqing No. 1 Intermediate People's Court held: The plaintiff, Chongqing Municipal People's Government, is entitled to file an ecological and environmental damage compensation lawsuit in accordance with the provisions of the "Notice of the General Office of the CPC Central Committee and the General Office of the State Council on Printing and Distributing the Pilot Plan for the Reform of the Ecological and Environmental Damage Compensation System" (Zhongban Fa [2015] No. 57). The plaintiff, Chongqing Liangjiang Volunteer Service Development Center, has qualified subject status for environmental public interest litigation. The subject status of both plaintiffs in bringing the lawsuit is not in doubt.

The Chongqing Municipal People's Government and the Chongqing Liangjiang Volunteer Service Development Center each enjoy their own right of action based on different provisions, both should be protected according to law. Accepting the two cases separately for filing is not improper. Given that the facts of the two cases are identical, the purpose of the litigation is the same, the defendants are the same, and the claims are substantially the same, it is more appropriate to consolidate the two cases for trial.

The disputed issues in this case are: 1. The relevance of the facts confirmed by the effective criminal judgment and the effective administrative judgment to this case; 2. Whether the types of pollutants, the exclusivity of pollution sources, the measurement of illegally discharged wastewater, and the quantified amount of damages determined in the "Appraisal and Assessment Report" are accurate; 3. Whether the defendants Cangjin Pavilion Company and Shouxu Company constitute joint infringement.

I. Regarding the relevance of the facts confirmed by the effective criminal judgment and the effective administrative judgment to this case

First, from the perspective of evidentiary effect, the facts confirmed by the effective criminal judgment and the effective administrative judgment can be directly confirmed as facts of this case, and there is no need to prove them by evidence in this case. Article 93 of the "Interpretation of the Supreme People's Court on the Application of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China" stipulates: "The following facts, the parties need not prove by evidence: ... (5) Facts that have been confirmed by a legally effective judgment of the people's court; ... For the facts specified in items (2) to (4) of the preceding paragraph, except where a party has sufficient evidence to the contrary to rebut them; for the facts specified in items (5) to (7), except where a party has sufficient evidence to the contrary to overturn them." The administrative judgment (〔2016〕Yu 0112 Xing Chu No. 324) and the criminal judgment (〔2016〕Yu 0112 Xing Chu No. 1615) are both effective judgments. The facts they confirm have res judicata effect and do not need to be proven again in this case, unless the defendant provides evidence to the contrary sufficient to overturn the original judgments. In this case, the defendants did not present any evidence, so the relevant facts are directly adopted. Moreover, since the administrative judgment (〔2016〕Yu 0112 Xing Chu No. 324) confirmed the legality of the Administrative Penalty Decision (Yu Huan Jian Fa [2016] No. 269) made by the Chongqing Environmental Supervision Team and the Administrative Reconsideration Decision (Yu Huan Fa [2016] No. 29) made by the Chongqing Environmental Protection Bureau, the said administrative decisions also have res judicata effect.

Secondly, this case is by nature a civil environmental tort case, which differs in the standard of proof and standard of liability required compared to criminal and administrative illegal cases. Therefore, the facts ultimately determined in this case, provided there is no contradiction, may differ from the facts determined in the criminal and administrative cases. The standard of proof and standard of liability in criminal cases are significantly higher than in civil cases. Where an environmental pollution crime causes damages, the responsible party should certainly bear the corresponding compensation liability. However, a polluting act not criminally convicted does not equate to not constituting a civil tort. In this case, the environmental pollution acts that should bear compensation liability according to law include, but are not limited to, the environmental pollution crimes determined in the criminal judgment (〔2016〕Yu 0112 Xing Chu No. 1615). Therefore, the defendants' objection that only the types of pollutants determined in the effective criminal judgment, i.e., total chromium and hexavalent chromium, should be the standard is untenable and is not supported. Regarding the facts confirmed in the effective administrative judgment, when the environmental protection department imposes administrative penalties for environmental pollution acts, it mainly relies on the national and local pollutant discharge standards. Violation of national and local mandatory standards warrants corresponding administrative penalties, and violation of mandatory standards is also a basis for the polluter to bear tort liability. However, although a polluting act that receives administrative penalties for violating mandatory standards is necessarily an environmental tort, an act that discharges pollutants in compliance with mandatory standards does not necessarily not constitute a civil tort. Article 1, Paragraph 1 of the "Interpretation of the Supreme People's Court on Several Issues Concerning the Application of Law in the Trial of Environmental Tort Liability Disputes" stipulates: "Where damage is caused by environmental pollution, regardless of whether the polluter is at fault, the polluter shall bear tort liability. Where the polluter claims not to bear liability on the ground that the discharge complies with national or local pollutant discharge standards, the people's court shall not support it." This provision indicates that the polluter cannot use compliance with mandatory standards as a defense to exempt from civil liability, meaning the scope of bearing civil liability for environmental pollution acts can be larger than the scope of administrative penalties. However, in this case, since the facts sued by the plaintiffs are the same as those confirmed in the effective administrative judgment, and they did not claim environmental torts beyond the scope of administrative violations, the facts of illegal discharge confirmed in the administrative judgment (〔2016〕Yu 0112 Xing Chu No. 324) can be used to determine the environmental tort facts in this case. However, this case will consider the constitutive elements, responsible parties, etc., from the perspective of environmental tort.

Third, combined with the facts confirmed by the effective criminal judgment and the effective administrative judgment, it can be determined that the defendant Shouxu Company directly implemented the environmental tortious conduct sued in this case. The reasons are: 1. The aforementioned effective administrative judgment and criminal judgment both confirm that the defendant Cangjin Pavilion Company, by signing the "Entrusted Operation Agreement" with Shouxu Company, entrusted all sewage discharge operations to Shouxu Company. During the operation of this project, Shouxu Company implemented the act of illegally discharging pollutants through concealed pipes. 2. Since Shouxu Company was the entrusted polluter, Cangjin Pavilion Company held the pollutant discharge permit and was the owner of the discharge equipment. Therefore, the discharge unit identified by the environmental protection department, i.e., the administrative counterpart, was Cangjin Pavilion Company. Based on this, an administrative penalty was imposed on Cangjin Pavilion Company. Although the target of the administrative penalty was Cangjin Pavilion Company, the administrative penalty decision and the administrative judgment did not deny the fact that Shouxu Company implemented the discharge act. Shouxu Company also participated in the administrative litigation as a third party. Moreover, it was precisely because Shouxu Company directly implemented the discharge act that the criminal judgment convicted and punished Shouxu Company and its directly responsible persons. 3. Regarding the discharge unit and the direct perpetrator identified in the effective administrative judgment and criminal judgment, both Cangjin Pavilion Company and Shouxu Company have no objection. In summary, it can be determined that the environmental tortious conduct implemented by Shouxu Company is the same fact of illegal discharge confirmed by the effective administrative judgment.

II. Regarding whether the types of pollutants, the exclusivity of pollution sources, the measurement of illegally discharged wastewater, and the quantified amount of damages determined in the "Appraisal and Assessment Report" are accurate

First, regarding whether the types of pollutants, the exclusivity of pollution sources, and the measurement of illegally discharged wastewater determined in the "Appraisal and Assessment Report" are accurate. The two defendants raised objections to the types of pollutants, the exclusivity of pollution sources, and the measurement of illegally discharged wastewater. These three aspects are basic facts determined by the environmental protection department when imposing administrative penalties and have been directly or indirectly confirmed by the administrative judgment (〔2016〕Yu 0112 Xing Chu No. 324). Moreover, Cangjin Pavilion Company has exercised its procedural rights according to law by applying for administrative reconsideration and filing an administrative lawsuit. In this case, the two defendants did not provide evidence to the contrary to overturn the original judgment. Therefore, the above environmental pollution facts relied upon by the "Appraisal and Assessment Report" are confirmed. Specifically: 1. Regarding the types of pollutants. Besides total chromium and hexavalent chromium determined in the effective criminal judgment, the wastewater illegally discharged by the two defendants also contained heavy metals such as total zinc and total nickel. This fact is confirmed by the environmental monitoring reports issued by the Jiangbei District Environmental Monitoring Station and the Chongqing Environmental Monitoring Center, as well as by the effective administrative judgment (〔2016〕Yu 0112 Xing Chu No. 324), and also by the investigative inquiry record of Cheng Long, legal representative of Shouxu Company, dated May 4, 2016. 2. Regarding the exclusivity of pollution sources. The two defendants argued that the sampling points W4 and W6 determined in the analysis report Jiang Huan (Jian) Zi [2016] No. JD009 issued by the Jiangbei District Environmental Monitoring Station were located higher than the Cangjin Pavilion wastewater treatment station, and therefore, the detection of pollutants exceeding standards at these two points could not have been caused by the acts of the two defendants. The court held that, given the fluid nature of water pollution, the appraisal institution was objectively unable to extract wastewater samples that flowed out during the continuous illegal discharge at the time around the wastewater treatment station. Therefore, it could only rely on the illegal discharge wastewater samples fixed by the environmental administrative law enforcement department through sampling when investigating the illegal acts of the two defendants for appraisal. Thus, the issue of whether the wastewater sampling underlying the "Appraisal and Assessment Report" was scientific essentially boils down to whether the sampling by the administrative law enforcement department during law enforcement was scientific. During the environmental law enforcement inspection of the Cangjin Pavilion wastewater treatment situation, several monitoring samplings were conducted. The selected sampling points included several rainwater outlets and several groundwater sampling points of Cangjin Pavilion Company, as well as the general wastewater outlet, the comprehensive collection tank of the wastewater treatment station, the chromium-containing wastewater regulating tank, the industrial park municipal outlet, and the outlet of Cangjin Pavilion municipal pipe network into the Yangtze River, etc. The points W4 and W6 mentioned by the defendants were respectively one rainwater outlet and one groundwater sampling point among the above. Besides the analysis report Jiang Huan (Jian) Zi [2016] No. JD009, the Jiangbei District Environmental Monitoring Station also issued monitoring reports such as Jiang Huan (Jian) Zi [2016] No. JD003, No. JD020, and No. JD034. The Chongqing Environmental Monitoring Center also issued monitoring reports such as Yu Huan (Jian) Zi [2016] No. SZD146, No. SZD150, No. SZD156, and No. SZD181. The administrative penalty decision of the Chongqing Environmental Supervision Team and the reconsideration decision of the Chongqing Environmental Protection Bureau were made based on a comprehensive assessment of the above monitoring reports, not solely on any single analysis report or monitoring report. The legality and reasonableness of the environmental protection department's actions in the entire administrative law enforcement process, including sampling and other preliminary procedures, have been confirmed by the administrative judgment (〔2016〕Yu 0112 Xing Chu No. 324) of the Chongqing Yubei District People's Court. At the same time, the above monitoring and analysis results show that the pollutants in the wastewater at the outlet of the industrial park and the municipal pipe network of Cangjin Pavilion Company into the river were heavy metal wastewater discharged from the electroplating industry. The report document Gong Guan Ban Wen [2016] No. 13 of the Chongqing Gangcheng Industrial Park Management Committee Office confirmed that Cangjin Pavilion is the only electroplating industrial park in the area involved, and the environmental monitoring results were consistent with the types of wastewater illegally discharged from the Cangjin Pavilion wastewater treatment station. The above facts prove that the source of the wastewater discharged from the above sampling points could only have come from the Cangjin Pavilion wastewater treatment station. Therefore, it can be determined that the pollutant source is exclusive. 3. Regarding the measurement of illegal discharge. The two defendants argued that they used several small holes with a width of less than 9 cm and a height of only 0.5-1 cm for self-flow seepage to discharge illegally, making it impossible to discharge 140,000 tons of wastewater during the alleged period. They also claimed that only No. 1 regulating tank had the illicit discharge situation, while No. 2 regulating tank did not. The court held that, based on the site layout plan of the Cangjin Pavilion wastewater treatment station, there is No. 1 comprehensive wastewater regulating tank and a chromium-containing wastewater regulating tank, but there is no "No. 2 wastewater regulating tank" as alleged by the defendants. According to the confirmation in the effective criminal judgment and administrative judgment, combined with the investigative inquiry records during the administrative law enforcement process, it can be determined that the wastewater from the chromium regulating tank entered the No. 1 comprehensive wastewater regulating tank, and the basic fact is that a 120mm diameter pipe network installed in the No. 1 tank was used to directly discharge wastewater containing heavy metals into the external environment and into the municipal pipe network. After court investigation, it was found that the "Appraisal and Assessment Report" was based on evidence such as the "Notice on the Determination of Sewage Discharge and Payment of Sewage Charges" (Yu Huan Fei Jiao Zi [2016] 0-4-1), the "Notice on the Determination of Recovery of Sewage Charges" (Yu Huan Fei He Zi [2016] 0-4-1), the investigative inquiry records made by the Chongqing Environmental Supervision Team respectively to the legal representative of Cangjin Pavilion Company, Sun Qiliang, and the legal representative of Shouxu Company, Cheng Long, and other evidence. It calculated the amount of illegally discharged wastewater by using the method of total water consumption minus consumption, sludge water content, online drainage volume, and holiday drainage volume. The underlying evidence and facts have either been recognized by the defendants or confirmed by effective judgments, or the relevant administrative actions have passed legality review in the administrative litigation procedure. The court confirms them all. The measurement method adopted is also in line with industry practice and is scientific and reasonable. Moreover, the plaintiffs issued the "Explanation on the Calculation of Illicit Discharge Amount and Sewage Charges of Cangjin Pavilion Company" to further explain the measurement basis and method. Therefore, it is determined that the two defendants illegally discharged 145,624 tons of wastewater. In summary, the objections raised by Cangjin Pavilion Company and Shouxu Company that the determination of pollutant types, amount of illegally discharged wastewater, and exclusivity of pollution sources were erroneous are untenable.

Second, regarding whether the quantified amount of damages determined in the "Appraisal and Assessment Report" is accurate. To prove the ecological and environmental damage consequences and the amount of compensation caused by the defendants' illegal discharge, the plaintiffs entrusted the Chongqing Academy of Environmental Sciences to conduct an appraisal and assessment of the ecological and environmental damage in this case. It issued the "Appraisal and Assessment Report," which determined that the quantified amount of ecological and environmental damage caused by the defendants' illegal discharge was RMB 14,416,776. Upon investigation, the Chongqing Academy of Environmental Sciences is an appraisal and assessment institution established in the "Notice of the Ministry of Environmental Protection on Printing and Distributing the 'List of Recommended Institutions for Environmental Damage Appraisal and Assessment (First Batch)'". Entrusting it to conduct the ecological and environmental damage appraisal and assessment in this case complies with Article 8 of the "Interpretation of the Supreme People's Court on Several Issues Concerning the Application of Law in the Trial of Environmental Tort Liability Disputes," which states: "For specialized issues related to ascertaining the facts of an environmental pollution case, a qualified judicial appraisal institution may be entrusted to issue an expert opinion, or an institution recommended by the competent department of environmental protection under the State Council may be entrusted to issue an inspection report, test report, assessment report, or monitoring data." It possesses the corresponding appraisal qualifications. According to the "General Outline of Technical Guidelines for Ecological and Environmental Damage Appraisal and Assessment" and the "Recommended Methods for Environmental Damage Appraisal and Assessment (Version II)" formulated by the Ministry of Environmental Protection, the hypothetical remediation cost method can be used in the appraisal and assessment to quantify the ecological and environmental damage caused by the incident, and the quantified results can serve as the basis for ecological and environmental damage compensation. Given that the defendants' illegal discharge acts lasted for a long time, the amount of illegal discharge was large, and the Yangtze River water body is in a state of flow, making it difficult to directly calculate the cost of ecological and environmental restoration, it is not improper for the "Appraisal and Assessment Report" to use the hypothetical remediation cost method to quantify the damage results. The hypothetical remediation cost refers to the expenditure that would be required to fully treat all pollutants currently discharged into the environment using current treatment technologies and levels, i.e., the product of the amount of pollutant discharge and the unit hypothetical remediation cost of the pollutant. Therefore, when the appraisal institution used the hypothetical remediation cost method, it was reasonable to take the wastewater treatment cost of RMB 22/ton actually paid by Cangjin Pavilion Company to Shouxu Company as the unit hypothetical remediation cost. Multiplying this by the amount of illegally discharged wastewater calculates the hypothetical remediation cost as RMB 3,203,728. The "Appraisal and Assessment Report" determined RMB 22/ton as the unit actual treatment cost based on the on-site verification of Cangjin Pavilion Company's financial vouchers by the Chongqing Environmental Supervision Team, combined with the investigative inquiry record of Sun Qiliang, legal representative of Cangjin Pavilion Company. The two defendants raised objections to this but did not produce any evidence to the contrary to negate it. According to the "Recommended Methods for Environmental Damage Appraisal and Assessment (Version II)", the principle for determining the cost of restoring Class III surface water pollution is 4.5 to 6 times the hypothetical remediation cost. Considering the pollution facts of this case, taking the minimum multiple of 4.5, the quantified amount of damages was calculated as RMB 3,203,728 × 4.5 = RMB 14,416,776, which is also not improper. In summary, the objection to the quantified amount of damages determined in the "Appraisal and Assessment Report" is rejected according to law.

In conclusion, environmental pollution dispute cases are highly professional and complex. In this case, the appraisal institution and the appraiser who issued the "Appraisal and Assessment Report" had qualified qualifications, the appraisal and assessment entrustment procedure was legal, the person in charge of the appraisal and assessment project also appeared in court as requested to be questioned, the facts underlying the appraisal and assessment were supported by effective legal documents, the calculation method and conclusions adopted were scientific and well-founded, and the two defendants failed to provide any evidence to rebut or overturn the "Appraisal and Assessment Report". Therefore, the "Appraisal and Assessment Report" and the related evidence it relies upon are all adopted.

III. Regarding whether the defendants Cangjin Pavilion Company and Shouxu Company constitute joint infringement

Defendant Shouxu Company was the direct implementing entity that knowingly exploited the 120mm-diameter pipeline network on the wall of No. 1 wastewater regulation tank and intentionally used it for illegal discharge. Its conduct caused environmental pollution, and it should naturally bear liability for compensation for the resulting damages. There should be no dispute on this point. The core issue of this point of contention lies in how to evaluate the conduct of Defendant Cangjinge Company and whether it and Shouxu Company constitute a joint tort. The court holds that Defendant Cangjinge Company and Shouxu Company constitute a joint tort and shall bear joint and several liability. The reasons are as follows: First, China implements a pollution discharge permit system, which is of significant importance for achieving达标排放 (compliance discharge) of industrial pollution sources. The pollution discharge permit is a means for the state to effectively manage dischargers, and can also be regarded as a contract between the government and the discharging entity. An enterprise that obtains a pollution discharge permit is a discharging entity and has the obligation to discharge pollutants according to law; otherwise, it shall bear corresponding legal liability. Cangjinge Company holds a pollution discharge permit issued by the competent administrative department, making it an enterprise eligible for discharging pollutants, but it must simultaneously ensure discharge in accordance with the requirements and standards of the permit. Cangjinge Company entrusted the wastewater treatment to Shouxu Company, a specialized environmental governance business (including industrial wastewater operation), through an entrusted operation agreement. Such conduct is not prohibited by law. However, whether discharging by itself or entrusting others to discharge, Cangjinge Company must ensure the normal operation of its wastewater treatment station and ensure that the discharged substances meet national and local discharge standards. This is a statutory duty of an enterprise that has obtained a pollution discharge permit, which cannot be relieved through civil agreements. In other words, as the discharging entity, Cangjinge Company has the statutory duty to supervise Shouxu Company's lawful discharge. According to the *Entrusted Operation Agreement*, it also has the obligation to monitor Shouxu Company's daily discharge situation. The illegal discharge in this case persisted for one year and eight months. Cangjinge Company clearly failed to fulfill its supervisory duty and shall bear liability for the consequences of environmental pollution.

Second, whether due to its statutory duty as the owner of the discharge equipment and the discharging entity, or according to the agreement between the parties, Cangjinge Company should ensure that the wastewater treatment facilities and equipment are normal and intact. In August 2014, when Cangjinge Company converted the waste acid tank into No. 1 wastewater regulation tank and changed the underground pipeline network to an overhead pipeline network, it failed to seal off the 120mm-diameter concealed pipe in the tank following normal treatment methods. Cangjinge Company also failed to provide evidence proving the reasonableness and legality of not sealing the concealed pipe. It was precisely through this concealed pipe that Shouxu Company carried out illegal discharge. That is to say, Cangjinge Company provided Shouxu Company with wastewater treatment equipment that retained a pipeline network capable of carrying out illegal discharge. Accordingly, it can be found that Cangjinge Company had intentional fault, and objectively provided conditions for the completion of the illegal discharge conduct.

Third, the wastewater to be treated was provided by Cangjinge Company to Shouxu Company. Therefore, Cangjinge Company knew the volume of wastewater requiring treatment. At the same time, as the discharging entity, Cangjinge Company was responsible for paying pollution discharge fees to the environmental protection department, and thus also knew the volume of wastewater that was legally discharged. Additionally, as the property management entity of the industrial park, it was also aware of the actual water usage of the enterprises in the park. By combining these data points, the existence of the illegal discharge conduct could be confirmed. Therefore, it can be held that Cangjinge Company knew that Shouxu Company was carrying out illegal discharge conducts, yet it condoned Shouxu Company's illegal discharge of wastewater and continued to entrust the wastewater to Shouxu Company for treatment. This can be regarded as forming an understanding with Shouxu Company, having joint intentional fault for the tort, and jointly causing the pollution consequences.

Fourth, environmental tort cases involve the composite nature of the method of infringement, the complexity of the infringement process, and the concealment and long-term nature of the consequences. The difficulty of proof, especially regarding the subjective intentional fault of the discharging enterprise for illegal discharge, is relatively high. Moreover, this case involves infringement of environmental public interests. Therefore, full consideration should be given to the particularities of such cases, and an accurate grasp of the burden of proof and the principle of imputation should be used to avoid evasion of liability and damage to public interests.

In summary, the defense of Cangjinge Company that it did not know Shouxu Company was illegally discharging pollutants and should not bear liability for compensation cannot be established and is not supported. Based on the facts and evidence of this case, the evidence that Cangjinge Company and Shouxu Company constitute a joint tort for environmental pollution has met the civil standard of proof of high probability. It shall be held that Cangjinge Company and Shouxu Company had subjective joint intentional fault and objective joint conduct for the illegal discharge. The two defendants constitute a joint tort. Pursuant to Article 8 of the *Tort Liability Law of the People's Republic of China*, which provides that "Where two or more persons jointly commit a tort causing harm to another person, they shall bear joint and several liability," the two defendants shall bear joint and several liability.

Plaintiff Chongqing Liangjiang Volunteer Service Development Center argued that this case also falls under the circumstance of a third party polluting the environment and that Article 5 of the *Interpretation of the Supreme People's Court on Several Issues Concerning the Application of Law in the Trial of Disputes over Liability for Environmental Torts* may be applied to order the two defendants to bear compensation liability. The court holds that since Cangjinge Company and Shouxu Company constitute a joint tort, the relevant provisions concerning environmental pollution by a third party are not applicable.

In addition to the quantified amount of ecological environmental damage as determined in the *Appraisal and Evaluation Report*, the two plaintiffs also made claims for fees such as appraisal fees and attorney fees. Article 22 of the *Interpretation of the Supreme People's Court on Several Issues Concerning the Application of Law in the Trial of Environmental Civil Public Interest Lawsuits* provides: "Where the plaintiff requests the defendant to bear expenses for inspection and appraisal, reasonable attorney fees, and other reasonable expenses incurred for the litigation, the people's court may support such claims in accordance with law." The plaintiffs claimed that the appraisal fee paid for this entrustment was RMB 300,000, but only provided a contract without documentation (invoices), and the amount manifestly exceeds the guiding price stipulated in the *Notice of Chongqing Municipal Price Bureau and Chongqing Municipal Bureau of Justice on Issuing the Catalogue of Judicial Assessment Fee Items Subject to Government Guided Pricing and Charging Standards in Chongqing*. That notice stipulates that for judicial appraisal involving property cases, fees are to be charged cumulatively in segments based on the subject matter amount: "(1) For amounts not exceeding RMB 100,000 (including RMB 100,000), fees shall be charged according to the standards listed in the annex to this notice. (2) For the portion exceeding RMB 100,000 up to RMB 500,000 (including RMB 500,000), 1% shall be charged. (3) For the portion exceeding RMB 500,000 up to RMB 1,000,000 (including RMB 1,000,000), 0.8% shall be charged. (4) For the portion exceeding RMB 1,000,000 up to RMB 2,000,000 (including RMB 2,000,000), 0.6% shall be charged. (5) For the portion exceeding RMB 2,000,000 up to RMB 5,000,000 (including RMB 5,000,000), 0.4% shall be charged. (6) For the portion exceeding RMB 5,000,000 up to RMB 10,000,000 (including RMB 10,000,000), 0.2% shall be charged. (7) For the portion exceeding RMB 10,000,000, 0.1% shall be charged." Considering that appraisal will inevitably generate corresponding expenses, combined with the actual circumstances of this case, and with reference to the guiding price of Chongqing, RMB 50,000 is determined on a discretionary basis. The *Guiding Standards for Attorney Service Fees in Chongqing* provide that for attorney representation fees in property-related cases, fees are charged cumulatively in segments based on the subject matter amount: "For the portion below RMB 100,000: 5%-6% (no less than RMB 5,000); for the portion from RMB 100,000 to RMB 1,000,000: 4%-5%; for the portion from RMB 1,000,000 to RMB 5,000,000: 3%-4%; for the portion from RMB 5,000,000 to RMB 10,000,000: 2%-3%; for the portion from RMB 10,000,000 to RMB 50,000,000: 1%-2%; for the portion above RMB 50,000,000: 0.5%-1%." The Chongqing Municipal People's Government and Chongqing Liangjiang Volunteer Service Development Center incurred attorney representation fees of RMB 198,000 and RMB 80,000 respectively for this litigation. The above fees were evidenced by contracts or invoices, and complied with the aforementioned provisions of the *Guiding Standards for Attorney Service Fees in Chongqing*. The two defendants also raised no objections. Therefore, this claim has factual basis and legal basis and is supported.

Regarding the claim added by Plaintiff Chongqing Liangjiang Volunteer Service Development Center during the trial requesting the two defendants to make a public apology, the court holds that the maintenance of the ecological system of the Yangtze River water area requires public participation. Acts of destruction committed against it would harm the interests of countless families and even future generations. The serious destructive conduct of the two defendants towards the ecological environment of the Yangtze River constitutes harm to the rights and interests of the general public. Requiring them to make a public apology is not only a manifestation of the lawful rights of the public, but also serves as a warning to other similar conduct. Furthermore, it can enable the two defendants to publicly express their profound understanding of their own faults and sincere repentance. Whether it is an environmental public interest lawsuit or an ecological environment damage compensation lawsuit, both have a public interest nature. In this case, the plaintiffs, on behalf of the general public, requested the tortfeasors of environmental pollution to apologize. This request is lawful and reasonable and is supported.

In conclusion, the facts of illegal discharge committed by Defendants Cangjinge Company and Shouxu Company as determined by the effective administrative judgment and criminal judgment are confirmed. The *Appraisal and Evaluation Report* is lawful and valid and is adopted as evidence. Cangjinge Company and Shouxu Company jointly committed illegal discharge conduct, causing damage consequences of environmental pollution, constituting a joint tort, and shall bear joint and several liability.

The First Intermediate People's Court of Chongqing, pursuant to Article 9 of the *Law of the People's Republic of China on Prevention and Control of Water Pollution*, Article 42(4) and Article 64 of the *Environmental Protection Law of the People's Republic of China*, Article 8 of the *Tort Liability Law of the People's Republic of China*, Articles 2 and 13 of the *Interpretation of the Supreme People's Court on Several Issues Concerning the Application of Law in the Trial of Disputes over Liability for Environmental Torts*, Article 22 of the *Interpretation of the Supreme People's Court on Several Issues Concerning the Application of Law in the Trial of Environmental Civil Public Interest Lawsuits*, and Article 64 and Article 142 of the *Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China*, on December 22, 2017, rendered the following judgment:

1. Defendants Chongqing Cangjinge Property Management Co., Ltd. and Chongqing Shouxu Environmental Technology Co., Ltd. shall jointly and severally compensate for the ecological restoration costs in the amount of RMB 14,416,776, to be paid into the designated account of the Chongqing Municipal Finance Bureau within ten days after this judgment takes effect, to be used by Plaintiff Chongqing Municipal People's Government and its designated departments, together with Plaintiff Chongqing Liangjiang Volunteer Service Development Center, for carrying out alternative restoration in light of the ecological environmental damage in this region;

2. Defendants Chongqing Cangjinge Property Management Co., Ltd. and Chongqing Shouxu Environmental Technology Co., Ltd. shall, within ten days after this judgment takes effect, make a public apology to society in provincial-level or above media;

3. Defendants Chongqing Cangjinge Property Management Co., Ltd. and Chongqing Shouxu Environmental Technology Co., Ltd. shall, within ten days after this judgment takes effect, pay Plaintiff Chongqing Municipal People's Government appraisal fees of RMB 50,000 and attorney fees of RMB 198,000;

4. Defendants Chongqing Cangjinge Property Management Co., Ltd. and Chongqing Shouxu Environmental Technology Co., Ltd. shall, within ten days after this judgment takes effect, pay Plaintiff Chongqing Liangjiang Volunteer Service Development Center attorney fees of RMB 80,000;

5. The remaining claims of Plaintiffs Chongqing Municipal People's Government and Chongqing Liangjiang Volunteer Service Development Center are dismissed.

After the first-instance judgment was rendered, none of the parties filed an appeal. This judgment has become legally effective.
